0.title: How to make your own DiscoX
0.content: The DiscoX is priced such that considering individual component postage and possible build mistakes it’s almost certainly cheaper to buy a DiscoX pre-built than to make your own. That said for anyone wanting to make one for fun or anyone curious. Here’s how a DiscoX is made. This is a work in progress, I’ll finish it after I’ve written the user instructions.

2.title: 3D printing an enclosure
2.content: The device has a latching button switch to control power to the device, press the button for at least 50ms to turn the device on and press it again to turn the device off.

3.content: Test Words . If the path to your favicon is /favicon.ico, you can leave favicon_ico unset.

5.title: Updating your software
5.content: The DiscoX software is always being improved. To keep your device working well and get the latest features, it’s a good idea to update it to the newest official version whenever you can. In this chapter, you’ll learn how to easily update your device so it keeps running smoothly.

6.title: Table of contents
6.content: . | Step 1: Download the lastest software | Step 2: Plug your DiscoX into your PC (in write mode) | Step 3: Copy across the new files | Step 4: Turn off/on | .

7.title: Step 1: Download the lastest software
7.content: The latest stable release can be found here: DiscoX Latest Stable. Once downloaded, right-click the downloaded zip-folder and select Extract All… to unzip its contents.

8.title: Step 2: Plug your DiscoX into your PC (in write mode)
8.content: When connected to your PC, your DiscoX mounts in Read-only mode by default. To enable Write mode for software updates, turn it on while holding the top button. Once mounted, you can relase the top button and it will appear in your file explorer, allowing you to edit or replace files.

9.title: Step 3: Copy across the new files
9.content: Copy all the extracted files to your DiscoX and choose Replace Existing when prompted.

10.title: Step 4: Turn off/on
10.content: Turn the DiscoX off and on again to activate the new software.

12.title: User Instructions
12.content: These are the the instructions for the latest firmware release, you may be using an older version of the DiscoX software on your device. To update to the latest version follow these instructions.

14.title: Buttons
14.content: The DiscoX has four buttons, labeled 1–4 in the image below. Pressing 1 takes a reading, 2 activates Disco mode, and holding 3 opens the settings menu. Button 4 turns the device on/off. In menu mode, buttons 1–3 have different functions: 1 moves up the menu, 2 moves down, and 3 selects an item.

15.title: Taking readings
15.content: To take a reading, press and hold button 1, or press it for longer than 100 ms (shorter presses are ignored). After you press the button, the DiscoX stays red until it detects the device is stable. Once stable, it turns green and records the reading. The DiscoX includes a leg-detection algorithm that triggers when it gets three consecutive readings where the compass, clino, and magnetometer values all fall within a set tolerance. When a leg is detected, the DiscoX flashes and beeps 3 times then turns purple.

16.title: Display
16.content: The display shows the data from your most recent reading. When Bluetooth is disconnected, readings are stored in memory. The count of stored readings appears next to the battery icon at the top of the screen.

17.title: Blutooth & memory
17.content: The DiscoX works with current versions of SexyTopo and TopoDroid. It’s always advertising over Bluetooth, so nearby devices will pick it up. Once connected, a BT icon appears in the top-left of the screen and you will be able to send live readings to your phone. If stored readings are present, the device will transmit them to your phone after connecting; this can take a few seconds, longer if many readings are queued. DO NOT turn the DiscoX off during this period or your readings will be lost. Feature request: In future versions of the software I’ll make it so you can save the latest 10 reading backup files to memory so you can retrive them if you run into connectivity/upload issues. Your DiscoX will come with a unique name e.g. DiscoX_Sasquatch, this name can only be changed by opening the case and programming the Bluetooth module directly. If you name a specific name in mind let me know and I can name it before assebling one.

18.title: Settings
18.content: There are two ways to change the DiscoX settings: using the onboard menu, or editing a more comprehnsive settings.toml file after connecting the device to your PC. To enter the onboard menu press and hold button 3. Enter Calibration . This puts the device into calibration mode, see calibration section. Anomoly detection . This checks for magnetic anomoies, e.g. putting the device too close to your helmet light, watch, srt kit or bolt. Sometimes gives false readings so can be turned off. Accuracy . With the current software version noise is supressed through averaing lots of readings, with the accuracy set high the device averages more readings before registering a shot. So it may be harder to take shots if you have a higher accuracy setting but your survey will be more accurate. Laser off . Having the laser on for long periods damages the laser and wastes battery, to prevent you from accidentally leaving it on you can make it automatically turn off after a set amount of time. Shutdown . This defines the amount of time of inactivity before the device is turned off.

19.title: The DiscoX
19.content: This website provides the most upto date technical infomation about the DiscoX cave survey device. The DiscoX is based on the SAP6 platform. The main differences being, the case design, user interface and microcontroller hardware.
